patch:
diff --git a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
index 1267cc2..295c2cb 100644
--- a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
+++ b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
@@ -57,6 +57,21 @@ Rules:
 - true, echo, printf, pwd, directory listings, and display-only reads are not completion checks.
 - Use replan when the current approach is wrong. Use stop only when blocked, unsafe, or impossible.
 - Keep rationale short. State the current fact and why the selected action changes or proves it.
+- Before your first execute, extract every explicit requirement from the ORIGINAL TASK (exact output
+  paths, filenames, formats, value ranges, CLI/API names, constraints) and keep them in plan. Before
+  finish, re-read the task and make the completion checks test each one literally against the saved
+  output, not merely that a command ran.
+- Hidden grading tests will probably use inputs different from the examples you can see. Prefer
+  general solutions over ones tuned to the visible sample, and exercise at least one edge case or
+  second input in a check when the task describes a general behavior.
+- Budget turns deliberately: start producing the real artifact within the first few turns, batch up
+  to four related commands per execute, and iterate. Aim to call finish by about 60% of the turn
+  budget so repairs remain possible. Do not spend turns re-reading files you have already seen.
+- Do not stop or give up because a tool or package is missing or a first approach fails. Try
+  alternatives (another installed tool, pip/apt if available, a pure-Python fallback) before using
+  stop. Stop is only for truly impossible or unsafe tasks.
+- If a run leaves background services or processes required by the task, confirm they are still
+  running in your completion check, since checks run in a fresh snapshot.
 """.strip()
 
 _REVIEW_RULES = """
